property_summary: After a Put call, the caller's unlock time must be at least the current block timestamp; the mutant fails to update it, leaving it possibly 0.

After a Put call with a future unlock time, the caller's unlock time must be >= the provided _unlockTime; the mutant fails to set it, so the unlock time remains unchanged (possibly less than _unlockTime).

For any caller, after a Put call the difference between the stored unlockTime and the max of the provided _unlockTime and block.timestamp must be zero; the mutant fails to update unlockTime, so this difference can be non-zero.
After any Put call with _unlockTime > block.timestamp, the caller's Acc[caller].unlockTime must equal _unlockTime; the mutant omits the assignment so unlockTime can differ.

The sum of all Acc balances plus the contract's Ether balance must equal the total Ether received (tracked by a public getter). In the reference, Acc balance increases by msg.value; in the buggy version, the Acc balance stays unchanged, breaking the invariant.
After a Put call, the caller's Acc balance must be at least msg.value greater than before the call; the bug removes the balance increment, violating this invariant.

After Put(msg.value > 0) via fallback, address(c).balance increases; in the bug, acc.balance does not increase, but the invariant that contract balance equals sum of all Acc balances plus tracked total received breaks only when an adversarial callee reverts on Collect, leaving Ether stranded and revealing the mismatch between actual Ether and recorded Acc balances.
After Put, the caller's Acc.balance must increase by msg.value; the mutant omits the increase, so after Put the caller's balance remains unchanged.

After any Put call, the sum of c.Acc[addr].balance over all addresses plus MinSum should equal address(c).balance in the reference (reentrancy lock prevents double-counting), but the bug can inflate acc.balance without corresponding Ether, breaking the invariant.
The contract allows an external reentrant caller to inflate its internal acc.balance without a matching Ether deposit.

After any sequence of calls, the sum of all account balances reported by Acc(...) plus the contract's own ETH balance must equal the total ETH ever deposited via Put/fallback; the bug allows an attacker to re-enter Put during Collect's external call, inflating their balance without depositing equivalent ETH, breaking this invariant.

After any sequence of calls, the balance recorded in c.Acc(msg.sender) for any address must be less than or equal to address(c).balance plus the total Ether paid out to that address via Collect, because each balance increment requires a matching deposit; the buggy nonReentrant_ modifier allows an attacker to re-enter Put during Collect's external call, recording multiple balance increments from a single deposit and violating this rule.
A successful call to Put must increase the caller's Acc balance by msg.value, but the bug causes Put to always revert, leaving the balance unchanged.
A successful call to Put must set the caller's unlockTime to the maximum of _unlockTime and block.timestamp, but the bug causes Put to always revert, so the stored unlockTime remains unchanged.

Any attempt to call Put, even with zero ETH, must revert on the buggy version due to assert(false), while the reference rejects only with invalid inputs; therefore after a call to Put with any valid parameters the transaction must succeed on the reference, but the buggy version always reverts the transaction.

The reference Put always succeeds and increases the caller’s Acc balance by msg.value, whereas the buggy modifier assert(false) makes every Put revert, so for any admissible parameters the reference transaction succeeds and the buggy one fails.

After a Put call with unlockTime > block.timestamp, the correct contract stores the supplied unlockTime, while the mutant always stores block.timestamp; this difference is observable via the public Acc mapping.

For any caller with at least MinSum balance and any am <= balance, a Collect after a Put that sets unlockTime in the future should not revert if the block.timestamp is after the recorded unlockTime, but the mutant stores block.timestamp instead of the future unlockTime, causing Collect to revert when it should succeed.

For any caller with enough balance and a future unlockTime, after the recorded unlockTime has passed, Collect must not revert; the mutant stores block.timestamp instead of the future time, causing Collect to revert when it should succeed because unlockTime never exceeds block.timestamp.

For any caller who calls Put with a future _unlockTime, the stored unlockTime must be that future value, not block.timestamp; the mutant always sets it to block.timestamp, so after the future time passes, the caller still cannot Collect because unlockTime is now in the past.

For any caller who calls Put with a future unlockTime, the Acc balance correctly increases by msg.value, but the bug corrupts the recorded unlockTime, and this balance increase is directly verifiable without needing to wait for unlock.
After a successful Collect call, the contract's balance must decrease by the collected amount.
